introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple and hears the seraphim cry, Holy, holy, holy. Purified, he answers God's call: Here I am, send me. In the Gospel, Peter lets down his nets at Jesus' word, catches a huge number of fish, and falls at his feet. Jesus says, Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching people. Let us answer the Lord's call, aware of our weakness and trusting his grace.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord calls us, sinners as we are, to follow him. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may put out into the deep and proclaim the Gospel with trust in Christ's word. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life: that many may answer, Here I am, send me. Let us pray to the Lord.
For fishermen and all whose work is hard and uncertain: that God may bless their labor. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel unworthy of God's call: that they may hear Jesus say, Do not be afraid. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that the grace of God given to us may not be in vain. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Holy God, you call sinners to be your messengers. Purify our lips and hearts, and give us the courage to follow your Son wherever he sends us. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Put out into the deep
reflection.body:
Isaiah sees a vision of God's holiness: the Lord on a high throne, the seraphim calling to one another, "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!" Faced with this holiness, Isaiah becomes aware of his own sin: "Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips." A seraph touches his lips with a burning coal, and he is forgiven. Then he hears God ask, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" And he answers, "Here I am. Send me!"

In the Gospel, Jesus teaches from Simon's boat. Then he tells him, "Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch." Simon is an experienced fisherman, and he knows the night was fruitless: "Master, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net." The catch is so large that the nets begin to tear and two boats nearly sink.

Simon's reaction is like Isaiah's. He falls at Jesus' knees: "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord." Close to the holiness of God, we see our own sin clearly. But Jesus does not send him away: "Don't be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive." They leave everything and follow him.

Paul, too, knows that he is unworthy. He persecuted the Church, yet he says, "But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile."

God does not wait for us to be worthy before he calls us. He calls us as we are and makes us what we need to be. This week, think about where Jesus may be asking you to put out into the deep, to try again where you have failed. And answer him, as Isaiah did: Here I am.
